meta.crs: EPSG:32610 local: x = easting - xmin, y = northing - ymin (meters)
meta.note: Educational comparison, not a prediction and not an official plan. A screening estimate of where street width binds and what widening or a parking change would take; not engineering, environmental review, appraisal or legal analysis. Counts only: no parcel identifiers, owners, addresses or imagery are stored; parcel and building geometry is fetched, counted in memory and dropped.

rules.hillSegment: model rule: drivable, Fire Zone 2–3 (City layer, or elevation ≥ 90 m beyond the city line), not a Lab private street, not closed by a barrier, pavement width measured (City pavement data or an OSM width tag)
rules.nominalParking: model rule: js/parking.js with seed null: both sides where they fit while leaving 8 ft, perfect parking, no bad parking jobs
rules.bindsEngine: model rule: nominal clear width under access.engineClearM (3.05 m, 10 ft; SB 99 p. 2–3)
rules.bindsTwoWay: model rule: nominal clear width under access.fireCodeClearM (6.1 m, 20 ft; CFC §503.2.1)
rules.engineReachLost: derived: Berkeley hill residents (BER- zones, Fire Zone 2–3 streets; js/sim.js engineReachStats) whose street an engine reaches within 5 minutes with no parked cars anywhere and does not when this pinch alone is closed to engines (js/sim.js engineTimes rules at ignition: Berkeley stations, 1.15 × posted speed, gates 3 min; a home counts at the nearer end of its segment). Synthetic expected residents, allocated as tools/access-constraints.mjs does
rules.engineReachGainNominal: derived: hill residents who come within 5-minute engine reach when this pinch alone becomes passable, every other segment in its nominal parking state
rules.choke: derived: the pinch is an entrance (chokeEdges) of an access-constrained area in data/model/access-constraints.json; residents behind = that area (synthetic)
rules.score: model rule: the larger of engineReachLost.people and choke.hillResidents
rules.grouping: model rule: adjacent binding segments of one street are one pinch when they enter the same choke area or their engine-reach losses are within 10%
rules.standards: engine: 10 ft clear plus 8 ft per side parked today (nominal); fireCode: 20 ft unobstructed (CFC §503.2.1) plus 8 ft per side parked today; full: two 10 ft lanes plus parking on both sides, 36 ft (assumption)
rules.strip: model rule: today's edge of pavement at half the City width from the County centerline; layouts: symmetric (half the gain each side) or all on one side; leastTaking = fewest buildings in the new pavement, then within the setback, then parcels, then retaining wall
rules.buildings: derived: OpenStreetMap footprints the new pavement reaches, and others within 3 m beyond it (assumption: a working setback); counts only
rules.parcels: derived: County parcel polygons the new strip enters (sampled every 1 m along and 0.25 m across); stacked polygons with the same outline (condominium units) count once; parcelsToAcquire counts parcels holding 1 m² or more of strip (assumption); stripInParcelsM2 = strip area inside any parcel (the rest lies in public right of way or unparceled land)
rules.sideSlopePct: derived: median over the pinch of the ground rise from today's edge of pavement to 6 m beyond it, per side (left = left of the County digitizing direction), from the 4 m DEM; positive uphill
rules.retainingWall: model rule: a wall where the ground 1 m beyond the new edge is 0.6 m or more above or below the centerline; wall face = that height along that length

cost.note: Pavement: the FDOT U19 all-in figure per m² of added pavement (low) and twice it (high, assumption: a small hillside job in the Bay Area). Retaining walls: where the ground 1 m beyond the new edge of pavement sits 0.6 m (2 ft) or more above or below the road centerline (DEM), a wall that tall along that stretch, priced from the WSDOT low (reinforced concrete wall, $70 per sq ft) to high (soldier pile tieback wall, $250 per sq ft) unit costs. Acquisition: each parcel holding 1 m² or more of the new strip is a partial take at 10–25% of the block group median home value (± the ACS margin of error); each building the new pavement reaches is taken whole at that value (step 2's rule). Red curb: $1–$4 per foot of curb for paint and signs (assumption; no public unit cost verified). Parked-car stall 6.7 m (22 ft, assumption). Left out: engineering, environmental review, legal costs, relocation benefits, utility poles and lines, drainage beyond the FDOT items, inflation since the figures' dates, and a contingency.

sb99.what: KLD TR-1380 SB 99 Access Impaired Neighborhood Analysis, Rev. 3 (2024-02-19), p. 2–3: 10 ft minimum travel lane, 8 ft per parked side

cfc.what: California Fire Code (2022) §503.2.1: fire apparatus access roads shall have an unobstructed width of not less than 20 feet

fdotU19.what: Florida DOT Cost Per Mile Models, U19 "Add 2 Lanes to Existing 2 Lane Undivided Arterial (1 Lane Each Side), with 4' Bike Lanes", curb and gutter, sidewalk, drainage and lighting: $9,540,676.51 per mile (October 2024 update), with 14,467.2 SY of new base per mile (12,096 m², 7.5 m of added width): $789 per m² of added pavement, all items included, flat terrain, no right of way
fdotU19.retrieved: 2026-11-01 (Wayback copy of 2025-10-06; listed on the cost-per-mile page also used by step 2)

wsdotWalls.what: WSDOT Bridge Design Manual M 23-50.24 (June 2025), Appendix 12.3-A1 Structural Estimating Aids, scoping-level unit costs updated April 2025 (mobilization included; no sales tax, engineering or contingency): reinforced concrete retaining wall $70–$110 per sq ft of exposed face; soldier pile wall $125–$170; soldier pile tieback wall $175–$250

acs.what: American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year, table B25077 median value of owner-occupied homes, by block group (Census Reporter API); block group from TIGERweb

parcels.what: Alameda County Parcel Boundaries (Parcels FeatureServer layer 0), geometry only; counted per pinch in memory and never saved

osm.what: OpenStreetMap building footprints (Overpass API; © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL); counted in memory and never saved

dem.what: USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM (Alameda County 2021), resampled to 4 m in data/terrain (bare earth)

step2.what: Egress step 2 (branch egress-candidates, PR #15, tools/egress-candidates.mjs): parcel counting from the County layer, block-group median home value from ACS B25077, partial takes at 10–25% of it, buildings taken whole
